$comment: Waypoints along the route: places worth photographing, places worth knowing
about, and places that are both. Coordinates are from OpenStreetMap unless a
note on the entry says otherwise.
Position along the trail is NOT stored here. The app projects each waypoint
onto the day's track at load time and derives distance-into-leg, elevation
and estimated arrival, so adding a waypoint only needs a name and a
coordinate. Anything more than 400 m from the day's track is treated as a
detour and shown with its own extra distance rather than as a point on the
roles:     photographic | historic, or both. Omitted means photographic,
which is what every waypoint was before landmarks existed.
A historic waypoint carries its writeup and sources in
data/history.json, keyed by this id; a photographic one carries
its photo block below. Neither is required of the other, so a
landmark nobody wants to photograph omits `photo` entirely.
kind:      col | lake | viewpoint | refuge | village | glacier | summit | heritage
bestLight: sunrise | morning | midday | afternoon | golden | sunset | blue | any
facing:    the direction you look to photograph the subject
priority:  1 = do not miss, 2 = strong, 3 = worth a frame if the light is there

waypoints.name: Statue du Christ-Roi
waypoints.$comment: Coordinate is the centre of OSM way 90540919; elevation from IGN RGE ALTI. Across the Arve from the route, so it projects onto the start of day 1 as a detour — see the writeup, which says so.

photo.subject: First reveal of the Bionnassay glacier and the Aiguille du Goûter
photo.notes: Reached within the first hour, so the light is still low and side-on. The tramway tracks make a strong leading line toward the glacier.

photo.subject: Séracs of the Glacier de Bionnassay above the Val Montjoie
photo.notes: A long lens compresses the icefall nicely. Contrast is harsh once the sun clears the ridge.

waypoints.name: Église de la Sainte-Trinité
waypoints.$comment: Coordinate is the centre of OSM way 98063406, traced from the French cadastre; elevation from IGN RGE ALTI.

photo.subject: Baroque chapel facade, then the Roman paved road climbing into the gorge
photo.notes: Deep in the gorge and shaded until late morning, which is ideal — the wet cobbles and torrent hold detail in flat light. Bring the tripod for a slow shutter on the cascades.

waypoints.name: Voie romaine des Rochassets
waypoints.$comment: Coordinate is the centre of the stone-surfaced OSM way 93907207 (name=Voie Romaine, surface=stone); elevation from IGN RGE ALTI. A point on the paved climb rather than a single object, so the exact metre is not meaningful.

photo.subject: Classic alpine chalet with pasture foreground
photo.notes: First real coffee stop. Cows and wildflowers in early July.

photo.subject: Wide glacial valley opening toward the Bonhomme cols
photo.notes: Last water and shelter before a long open climb. Good spot to shoot the group small against the valley.

waypoints.name: Plan des Dames
waypoints.$comment: Coordinate is the centre of OSM way 1428087777 (historic=archaeological_site, archaeological_site=tumulus). Its OSM ele tag of 2043 m and IGN RGE ALTI at 2044 m agree, which is reassuring for a cairn rather than a surveyed point.

photo.subject: Stark rock-and-scree panorama, often with snow patches into July
photo.notes: Exposed and frequently windy. A polariser helps with the haze looking back over the Beaufortain.

waypoints.name: Col de la Croix du Bonhomme

photo.subject: High point of day 2, with the Mont Blanc massif stacked behind the ridges you just crossed
photo.notes: The trail tops out near 2,479 m just past the refuge. Afternoon light rakes across the ridgelines and separates the layers — a natural spot for a long-lens compression shot.

waypoints.name: Refuge du Col de la Croix du Bonhomme

photo.subject: Refuge perched on the col
photo.notes: If the group ever chooses to sleep here instead of descending, sunset from the col is exceptional.

waypoints.name: Les Chapieux
waypoints.$comment: Coordinate is OSM node 440903287 (place=hamlet, wikidata=Q20108329); elevation from IGN RGE ALTI, which puts it 7 m below the OSM ele tag of 1560.

photo.subject: Converted dairy farm at the head of the Vallée des Glaciers
photo.notes: Where the walking starts on the shortcut day. The climb to Col de la Seigne begins immediately behind.

photo.subject: The single best reveal on the tour — the entire Italian side of Mont Blanc, with the Aiguille Noire de Peuterey and the Brouillard face
photo.notes: You crest the France–Italy border and the south face of Mont Blanc appears all at once. Get here early: morning light is still front-lighting the face and the valley haze has not built. Budget real time here, not a snack stop.

waypoints.name: La Casermetta
waypoints.$comment: Coordinate and elevation from the OSM node tagged La Casermetta (alpine_hut, ele=2365), which matches the 2,365 m in the Espace Mont-Blanc document and falls within 20 m of the day-3 track vertex at that height, about 800 m past the col.

photo.subject: Refuge tucked beneath the Glacier de la Lée Blanche and the Pyramides Calcaires
photo.notes: The refuge reads small against the icefall — include it for scale. The Pyramides Calcaires are an unusual pale limestone against all that granite.

photo.subject: Braided outwash flats and shallow lakes reflecting the Mont Blanc south face
photo.notes: The reflection is the shot. Wind flattens it — still water is a morning phenomenon, so this rewards an early start or an overnight nearby. Get low to double the mountain in the water.

photo.subject: Val Veni behind, Courmayeur below
photo.notes: Looking back down the whole valley you have just walked. Good end-of-day summary frame.

photo.subject: Characterful hut at the col with the Grandes Jorasses on the skyline
photo.notes: Famous for its terrace. A cold drink here is traditional.

photo.subject: Balcony viewpoint straight across to the Grandes Jorasses
photo.notes: Start of the Val Ferret balcony traverse. On the shortcut day the bus skips this — worth an evening walk up from Courmayeur if the light looks good.

photo.subject: The postcard Grandes Jorasses panorama, with Mont Blanc's Italian ridges running left
photo.notes: One of the great refuge views in the Alps. The Jorasses catch first light while the valley stays blue — a genuine reason to be here at dawn rather than midday.

photo.subject: Head of the Italian Val Ferret where the climb to Grand Col Ferret begins
photo.notes: Top of the Val Ferret bus line, and the start of walking on the shortcut day.

photo.subject: Glacier de Pré de Bar tumbling down directly opposite
photo.notes: The most accessible close-up glacier view of the tour. Last real stop before the col.

photo.subject: Highest point of the classic route. Italy on one side, the Swiss Val Ferret on the other
photo.notes: Turn around at the top — the retrospective down Italian Val Ferret to the Mont Blanc massif is better than the forward view. Border-crossing group shot belongs here.

photo.subject: Small resort lake with the Grand Combin group on the skyline
photo.notes: Arrival-evening shot. Calm water at dusk and a very civilised place to be holding a camera.

photo.subject: High pasture with the Rhône valley and Martigny far below
photo.notes: The big open view on the Bovine route. A completely different landscape register from the glacier days — pastoral, hazy, layered.

photo.subject: Road col above Trient
photo.notes: Hotel and shop. Descend from here to Trient.

photo.subject: The Trient Glacier head-on from a knife-edge notch at 2,665 m
photo.notes: The standout photographic objective of the Swiss section and the highest point of the whole tour. Only on the Arpette variant, which trades roughly 400 m of extra climbing and a boulder-field descent for it. Needs settled weather and no lingering snow — decide the night before.

photo.subject: The bright pink neo-gothic church against dark forested slopes
photo.notes: Unmistakable and slightly absurd. A saturated colour accent in an otherwise green-and-grey valley.

photo.subject: The full length of the Chamonix valley with Mont Blanc centred at the head of it
photo.notes: The great closing view of the tour and arguably the best single composition on the route — the valley funnels the eye straight to the summit. Old refuge on the border makes a foreground anchor. Haze builds through the day, so earlier is better.

photo.subject: Ridge walk with the Argentière glacier basin and the Aiguille Verte opposite
photo.notes: On the main route rather than the Le Tour shortcut. A rare spot where the trail itself is the subject — the ridge line leads into the frame.

photo.subject: Hamlet at the head of the Chamonix valley under the Tour glacier
photo.notes: Where the shortcut day finishes and the bus back to Chamonix starts.

photo.subject: The famous steel ladder and rung section up the Aiguillette d'Argentière slabs
photo.notes: Only on the classic final stage. Dramatic verticality and a great place to shoot people for scale, but it is a scramble — secure the camera before starting up.

photo.subject: The most photographed reflection in the Alps — the Aiguille Verte, Les Drus and Mont Blanc mirrored in the lake
photo.notes: Roughly 900 m off the main route above La Flégère, so it is a deliberate detour with a real climb attached. The reflection needs still air, which in practice means sunrise or late evening; the refuge beside the lake takes bookings and is the only way to be there for that light. Often still partly frozen in early July, which is its own picture.

photo.subject: Balcony traverse looking straight across at the Mer de Glace and the Aiguilles de Chamonix
photo.notes: Lift station, so it doubles as a bail-out point down to Chamonix. The whole massif is laid out opposite — a panorama stitch works well here.

photo.subject: The head-on Mont Blanc panorama, directly facing the summit across the valley
photo.notes: The classic Chamonix viewpoint and the last high ground of the tour. Alpenglow on the summit from here is the trip's natural closing frame. Cable car down if legs are finished.

photo.subject: Small refuge on the final descent with Mont Blanc still filling the frame
photo.notes: Last stop on the classic route before the long drop to Les Houches.
